author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Two raccoons found in populated Warwick neighborhoods tested positive for rabies, bringing Rhode Island’s 2026 total to 34 confirmed rabid animals, the Department of Health said.

One raccoon was found near Walter Street and the other near Duncan Road. Three adults and two dogs connected to the Walter Street area received treatment, while another dog was treated after a possible exposure near Duncan Road.

The statewide count already exceeds the average of 24 rabid animals reported annually from 2021 through 2025. Health officials said 43 people have received treatment after exposure this year. The confirmed animals include 20 raccoons, 10 bats, one cat, one coyote, one skunk and one woodchuck.

RIDOH advises residents not to approach or feed wild or free-roaming animals and to keep dogs, cats and ferrets current on rabies vaccinations. Anyone who may have had direct contact with either raccoon should contact RIDOH promptly for an exposure assessment. Possible pet exposures should be reported to the department, local animal control and a veterinarian.
dek: The state’s 2026 total already exceeds the recent annual average, and health officials are urging residents to avoid contact with wildlife.
headline: Rhode Island rabies count reaches 34 after two Warwick raccoons test positive
